drivingQuestion: Does R' Yehuda's view bind Rava's ruling?
outcomeNote: Rava sets aside R' Yehuda as a rejected minority view

segments.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: הָא אֲנַן תְּנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם קִבְּלָה הֵימֶנּוּ בְּמָעוֹת – בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אֵינוֹ מְנַכָּה לוֹ מִן חֲכוֹרוֹ! אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֵית דְּחָשׁ לַהּ לִדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: The Gemara continues the story: «The Rabbis said to Rava: Didn’t we learn» in the mishna here: «If» the cultivator «received it from» the owner «for» a fixed sum of «money, whether this» way or «whether that» way, i.e., whether a regional disaster occurred or not, «he does not subtract» the produce he owes as part of «his tenancy.» Rava «said to them: There is no» one «who is concerned for» the ruling «of Rabbi Yehuda» since it is a minority opinion that is rejected.
